media.alt: World Blood Donor Day - Giving blood saves lives voluntary donors have the lowest incidence of Hepatitis B and C

content.text: "Out of all blood donors, 25 percent are voluntary, who have the lowest incidence of Hepatitis B and C, while commercial donors have the highest percentage of this disease," revealed Dr Khalid Zafar Hashmi, President of the Pakistan Society for Haematology, at the World Blood Donor Day, organized at Aga Khan University. This day commemorates the birth anniversary of Karl Landsteiner, founder of the blood group system and Nobel laureate.

Speaking on Donor Motivation, Dr Hashmi called for increased voluntary donor recruitment and outlined factors that motivate potential donors, such as information and persuasion, dispelling unfounded fears, and benefits to donors. Dr Hashmi disclosed interesting findings of a study in Finland, which showed that blood donors had an 80 percent lower risk of heart attack compared to non-donors.

Other speakers included Mr Anwar Ajanee, Chairman of Karachi Lions Aga Khan University Hospital Blood Bank Committee and AKU's Haematologists: Dean Dr Muhammad Khurshid, Dr Bushra Moiz, and Dr Salman N. Adil.

Speaking on Safe Blood Donation, Dr Bushra Moiz highlighted the fact that over 30,000 women die each year during pregnancy or delivery in Pakistan. Calling for the development and implementation of a national blood transfusion policy, she mentioned that there is a serious shortage of safe blood in the country, and emphasized the importance of developing systems for strong laboratory quality assurance practices, and using the correct methodologies for proper screening.
Stressing on the voluntary aspect of organizing blood donations by Karachi Lions, Mr Anwar Ajanee mentioned that from 1986, Rs. 2.3 million have been spent on setting up Camps.

Ms Asma Mumtaz Channa, a former patient of the University Hospital and blood recipient, compared blood to divine gifts like water, and listed various circumstances under which blood is needed. She expressed her deep thanks to the doctors and staff of the Haematology Department of AKUH.

Mr Firoz Rasul, President of Aga Khan University and Chief Guest on the occasion, thanked the Karachi Lions for their efforts, and said that blood donation is an unselfish act that in many instances enables others to live. He hoped that members of the audience would be encouraged to donate blood.
Aga Khan University Hospital ensures that the highest standards are in place to ensure timely and safe blood supply to its patients.
